A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Harmony and provide readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices A–F. Visual inspection resolved extraction problems with rotated table headings and graphical content, supporting a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original pre-training and downstream evaluations, including classification, segmentation, detection, retrieval, component ablations, and appendix experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains original downstream and ablation results and adds model-scaling, batch-size, and approximately compute-matched comparisons.

M1.justification: The five-objective architecture remains intact, but the stated soft-contrastive loss changes in Equation 4: v2 replaces raw teacher similarities with explicitly normalized A_V/A_T targets and uses the student temperature for student predictions. This establishes a limited revision to the reported objective; whether the implementation changed is unspecified.

E1.justification: Training and evaluation coverage is retained, including CC3M, ImageNet-1k, ADE20K, COCO, Flickr30K, and the additional zero-shot datasets. Table 2 drops its duplicate ImageNet-1k column, but that evaluation remains in Table 1. Retrieval moves to Appendix B, and the YFCC15M instability account remains in Appendix F.

E2.justification: v2 Table 1 adds SigLIP as an evaluated comparator at small and base sizes. The existing comparator families—MAE, iBOT, CLIP, SLIP, and MaskCLIP—are retained.

E3.justification: v2 adds base-size configurations for existing baselines and a large-model Harmony/CLIP comparison. The reported component-ablation batch size changes from 512 to 768, and ViT-B local crops change from six to eight. The new compute comparison varies training epochs and batch sizes to approximately match resources, selecting the best zero-shot checkpoint from checkpoints saved every ten epochs.

E4.justification: v2 adds substantial analyses of relative model-size scaling, batch-size sensitivity, and whether Harmony's advantage persists under approximately matched computing budgets. It revises the component-ablation results and removes v1 Appendix B's memory/time-versus-batch-size analysis. The MaskCLIP, masking-scheduler, augmentation, attentive-masking, and qualitative appendix analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports seed or replicate counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or statistical significance tests. Results remain point estimates; the added experiments introduce no uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Many main, ablation, zero-shot, and retrieval values are revised; for example, Table 1's Harmony-S zero-shot accuracy changes from 21.0 to 20.8. v2 adds baseline configurations, compute-controlled results, batch-size results, and ViT-L accuracies of 26.5 for Harmony versus 20.3 for CLIP in Figure 3. The old memory-profiling results disappear. Changed or unspecified settings limit direct before–after performance comparisons.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 adds formal definitions for A_V and A_T using softmax(P(...; teacher temperature)) and revises Equation 4's targets and temperature placement. This is a mathematical change beyond notation. The remaining loss formulations are substantively retained, with no new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain unchanged. The abstract shifts its stated performance comparison from ViT-S/16 to ViT-B, while the new introductory Figure 1 claims that small Harmony exceeds base-size comparators on linear-probed classification and detection and emphasizes scaling advantages.

C2.justification: v2 interprets widening model-size performance gaps as better scaling and the compute-controlled comparison as evidence that additional resources alone do not explain Harmony's advantage. It also discusses baseline plateauing and overfitting during longer training. Existing feature-complementarity explanations and mixed-precision failure limitations largely remain.

D1.justification: Appendix A adds ViT-L hardware information—sixteen 80 GB A100 GPUs for about a day—and revises ViT-B hardware from 24 V100s to 8–16 V100s. Table 4 defines its resource measurements. Conversely, v2 omits v1's explicit ViT-B batch size of 912, some vision-encoder specifications, and the old memory-profiling recipe. Code-access information is unchanged.

R1.justification: The related-work narrative, cited works, and novelty positioning are retained. Numbered citations become author–year citations and bibliography formatting changes. SigLIP appears as an experimental comparator without an accompanying expansion of related-work discussion.

P1.justification: Most exposition and section organization are retained. v2 updates affiliations and citation style, abbreviates loss names, reorders contribution bullets, moves retrieval discussion to Appendix B, and adds focused scaling and compute-comparison passages.

P2.justification: v2 adds performance-overview and scaling plots, recolors the architecture diagram, and substantially redesigns the main tables, including replacing rotated dataset headings with horizontal headings. It adds compute and batch-size tables, relocates retrieval, removes the old profiling table, and changes the title block, typography, and page styling.

improvement.justification: The larger-model comparisons and approximately compute-matched evaluation in v2 Tables 1 and 4 strengthen the empirical case beyond v1's mainly equal-epoch comparisons. These benefits outweigh limited losses in documentation, but some configuration details disappear and results are not fully reconciled: CLIP segmentation is 35.3 in Table 1 versus 36.5 in Table 3, whereas the corresponding v1 tables agree. The net improvement is modest.
